issues.description: The problem text explicitly requires Farm to store animals using a Set implemented as a HashSet (ensuring uniqueness), but the provided solution implements the Farm.animals attribute as a List and initializes it with an ArrayList. This divergence between the specification and the solution can confuse students about which collection type to use and which semantics (uniqueness, ordering) are expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Either (A) update the solution (and template) to use a Set<Animal> and initialize it with a new HashSet<>() in the no-arg constructor (and adjust get/set/add methods accordingly), or (B) change the problem text to require a List/ArrayList if ordering/duplicates are intended. Prefer option A to match the explicit textual requirement for uniqueness.

issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction: the UML excerpt shows Farm.animals typed as List<Animal>, while the textual instructions later state that the aggregation should be realized using a Set implemented with a HashSet. This inconsistency leaves students unclear whether to implement the Farm collection as a List or as a Set.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and unify the problem statement: update the UML diagram to show Set<Animal> (and mention HashSet in the diagram or notes) if uniqueness is required, or change the textual instruction to require a List if duplicates/ordering are intended. Ensure template and solution examples follow the same choice.
